title: Linux - Hardening Overview
html:
Linux Hardening

Use this section to investigate Linux hosts, understand privilege boundaries, and review the controls that constrain local access. Start with the Linux basics and the privilege escalation checklist for a general assessment, then follow the relevant topic below.

  • Linux basics: privilege escalation methodology, useful commands, environment variables, and restriction bypasses.
  • Main system information: kernel, modules, sudo, filesystem behavior, jails, and the escalation checklist.
  • User information: Linux identities, groups, SSH agent forwarding, and Active Directory integration.
  • Interesting files and permissions: writable paths, capabilities, SUID behavior, NFS, wildcard expansion, and SELinux.
  • Network information: local services, sockets, and network-related exploitation examples.
  • Software information: authentication modules and application-specific attack surfaces.
  • Processes, crontab, systemd, and D-Bus: scheduled execution and interprocess communication.
  • Containers and namespaces: runtimes, isolation boundaries, and container hardening.
  • Post-exploitation: credential discovery, persistence, and host-level follow-up techniques.
